asof: Results as of the morning of Nov. 4, 2026. Counts are unofficial: Ohio's canvass takes about three weeks, Kansas's governor race is uncalled, and several Congress and legislature counts are still moving. Items marked Reported or Unconfirmed rest on thinner sourcing.
lede: Voters made data centers a campaign issue in 2026, and the results point one way: more scrutiny, more cost rules and more local vetoes. Most of what changes starts in January, when new governors and a new Congress take office. Until then, sitting governors and lame-duck legislatures keep their powers. This tab separates what has happened from what is promised, and flags where the evidence is thin.
tiles: governor races in our pre-election data center table went to Democrats; Florida was the exception
Democratic majority on Georgia's utility commission, flipped Nov. 3; Louisiana's stays Republican
chambers of Congress reported flipping to Democrats; final seat counts still being settled

effects.t: Texas elects Hinojosa, who ran on a data center moratorium
effects.b: Democrat Gina Hinojosa beat three-term Gov. Greg Abbott. She wants new approvals halted until lawmakers pass community protections, plus union hiring, limits on nondisclosure deals and an end to tax breaks. She takes office Jan. 19.
effects.how: Texas holds roughly a quarter of planned U.S. data center capacity, so a pause here matters most. Whether a governor can halt grid connections alone is disputed, and ending tax breaks needs the Legislature.

effects.t: Abbott's permit freeze and grid audit carry Texas to the handover
effects.b: Abbott began pausing data center approvals in August, first at the grid operator and then at the environmental permitting agency, while an audit runs until about December. Advocates say some permits were approved anyway. No end date for the freeze has been announced.
effects.how: The freeze bridges to Hinojosa's Jan. 19 start unless Abbott lifts it as a lame duck, which has not been reported. The December audit result is the next marker.

effects.t: Texas Legislature likely divided, which caps how far a pause can go
effects.b: Reports say Democrats gained the Texas House while Republicans keep the Senate. Seat counts are unofficial and the exact figures are not confirmed. Abbott has said he also wants to change data center tax breaks.
effects.how: A statutory moratorium would struggle in the Senate, but tax-break changes and ratepayer bills look negotiable in the 2027 session.

effects.t: Ohio elects Acton, who backs a conditional moratorium
effects.b: Democrat Amy Acton beat Vivek Ramaswamy and succeeds term-limited Gov. DeWine. Her plan pauses new projects until developers cover their energy costs, bring their own power, use union labor and meet environmental standards, with clawbacks on incentives.
effects.how: Ramaswamy's day-one executive order pledge is moot. Acton can appoint utility regulators and shape agency rules from January, but most of her plan needs the Republican-led General Assembly. The official canvass is still weeks away.

effects.t: Ohio lame-duck bills could limit the next administration's data center rules
effects.b: An advocacy group says lawmakers are weighing bills that would constrain how a new administration writes data center rules, and that leaders may seek a legislative veto over agency rules. No votes have been reported. This is the group's characterization, not independent reporting.
effects.how: If passed before January, rulemaking power over data centers could shift away from Acton. Watch the lame-duck calendar.

effects.t: Sherrod Brown beats Husted after calling him the face of data centers
effects.b: Brown defeated Sen. Jon Husted, who led the Senate push for the Ratepayer Protection Act. One group notes only 3% of Ohio Senate voters named data centers as their top issue, so how much the issue decided the race is contested.
effects.how: Both parties now treat data center power costs as a campaign liability heading into 2028, which raises the bar for any federal bill that only encourages states to act.

effects.t: Georgia elects Bottoms, who pledged a statewide pause
effects.b: Keisha Lance Bottoms beat billionaire Rick Jackson, ending more than 20 years of Republican control of the governorship. She proposed a pause on new data center construction followed by a review, and said a pause would be a first priority, though she was unsure it could be done by executive order.
effects.how: A governor-led pause push now pairs with a Democratic utility commission. Statutory changes would face the Republican legislature.

effects.t: Democrats win control of Georgia's utility commission
effects.b: Peter Hubbard and Shelia Edwards won the two seats on the ballot, making the five-member commission 3 to 2 Democratic for the first time in about 30 years. Campaigns centered on rate increases and rural data center growth. The seat Edwards wins was held by a commissioner who now works for a data center builder.
effects.how: The commission sets Georgia Power's rates and approves its power plants. The new majority takes over before Georgia Power's long-term plan update and a rate case, the first since 2022, both expected from 2027.

effects.t: Google's nuclear uprate deal with Georgia Power now goes to a Democratic commission
effects.b: The deal adds about 96 MW through uprates at the Hatch plant and was announced in September. Georgia Power puts lifetime customer benefits near $900 million. The commission still has to approve the Hatch uprate.
effects.how: A clean-power, ratepayer-protective deal is more likely approved than rejected, but its terms could draw sharper questions from the new majority in 2027.

effects.t: Louisiana's utility commission stays Republican, widening its edge to two seats
effects.b: Republicans Stephanie Hilferty and John Atkins won the two open seats. The outgoing commissioners are expected to cast their last vote on Meta's Hyperion project at the Nov. 18 meeting, before the new members are sworn in.
effects.how: Little policy change is expected for the Entergy and Meta Hyperion build-out.

effects.t: Wisconsin elects Crowley and gives Democrats full control
effects.b: David Crowley narrowly beat Tom Tiffany. He backs pausing data center construction until a state DNR environmental review is finished and says he would sign a repeal of data center tax exemptions. Reporting says Democrats now hold both chambers and the governorship for the first time in 16 years.
effects.how: A statutory pause and tax-exemption repeal become plausible in the 2027 session. Crowley takes over from the retiring Gov. Evers in January.

effects.t: Michigan elects Benson and a Democratic trifecta
effects.b: Jocelyn Benson won. She favors guardrails on noise and electricity costs rather than a ban. Reporting says her win keeps the clean energy mandate and a governor-appointed utility commission overseeing DTE's and Consumers' large investment plans.
effects.how: Expect 2027 bills on ratepayer protection and siting in a state that is already a battleground over large-load contracts.

effects.t: Pennsylvania Democrats flip the state Senate, giving Shapiro a trifecta
effects.b: Shapiro won reelection and Democrats took the state Senate for the first time in nearly 50 years. The source does not discuss data centers directly.
effects.how: Shapiro, who backs data centers but has tied them to ratepayer protections and local approval, now has votes for large-load tariff and siting bills in 2027.

effects.t: Kansas governor's race, run partly on a data center pause, is too close to call
effects.b: Cindy Holscher, who ran on a statewide pause, led Ty Masterson by about 5,500 unofficial votes. Masterson has not conceded and AP has not called it. A recount is possible. Democrats also broke the Republican supermajority in the state House.
effects.how: If the lead holds, Kansas gets a pause-minded governor facing a Republican legislature without a veto-proof majority.

effects.t: New Hampshire's Ayotte wins a second term after shifting toward a moratorium
effects.b: NBC projects Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte beat Democrat Cinde Warmington, who ran on a temporary moratorium on large data center permits. Ayotte has said she plans a multi-year moratorium in her budget.
effects.how: One of few Republican governors in a competitive state to hold on. A budget-based pause stays on the table for 2027.

effects.t: Democrats retake Congress, gaining subpoena power over AI and energy
effects.b: CBS reports Democrats won at least 54 Senate seats and Roll Call counted 29 House flips as of midday Nov. 4, with several races uncalled. House Democrats hold leadership elections Nov. 18 and the new Congress is seated Jan. 3. Data center campaigns helped flip Pennsylvania and Colorado House seats, though opened sources do not tie each race to the issue.
effects.how: Democrats gain oversight and hearing power on data center load growth, ratepayer costs and AI companies. A Trump veto still blocks most legislation.

effects.t: Pallone expected to chair House Energy and Commerce
effects.b: Search coverage says Frank Pallone is poised to chair the committee and has opposed blanket moratoriums, preferring to learn from state and local approaches. Chairs are not final until the caucus votes. Another outlet reports some Democrats want a temporary federal construction moratorium.
effects.how: Expect oversight of data center load growth and ratepayer impacts from January, but a federal moratorium looks unlikely.

effects.t: Lame-duck session decides whether the Senate permitting deal passes before Democrats take the House
effects.b: Negotiators unveiled a bipartisan affordability and permitting package on Sept. 30 that would make data centers pay transmission costs tied to their demand. Senate Democrats must decide whether to advance it now or wait. The Dec. 11 funding deadline is the forcing event.
effects.how: If it passes in December, the cost-allocation provisions become law first. If not, the fight restarts in 2027 on Democratic terms.

effects.t: Federal preemption of state AI laws gets harder
effects.b: Time reports the push to bar state AI regulation faces tougher odds with Democrats in power, though Democrats would also struggle to override a Trump veto of broader AI rules. No White House statement on preemption followed the election. The administration's December 2025 order directing litigation against state AI laws remains its main tool.
effects.how: Preemption through must-pass bills such as the defense bill is now unlikely. The fight shifts to Justice Department suits against state laws.

effects.t: AI industry super PACs underperform; pro-safety groups outspent them in key races
effects.b: Per Time, Leading the Future mostly held back after donors pulled back, while pro-safety PACs outspent accelerationist ones in several races. Musk spent at least $474 million across the cycle, including $168 million for Paxton, who lost. Results for the pro-data-center PAC Building the Future were not found.
effects.how: Weakens the electoral case for AI industry money. Three-quarters of likely voters said they would be less likely to back a candidate who takes AI super PAC money.

effects.t: California's AI laws become the de facto national standard if Congress stalls
effects.b: Time quotes a Carnegie analyst arguing that gridlock in Washington leaves California's rules, including the first U.S. frontier-AI law, to govern in practice. Becerra won the governor's race easily.
effects.how: Lowers near-term odds that federal action overrides California. The 2027 session is the next test.

effects.t: Local ballot measures went against data centers almost everywhere
effects.b: CNBC, citing Ballotpedia, reports 41 local measures in 10 states, with Ohio holding 21. Voters sided against data centers in every measure with results except Harwood, North Dakota, where a charter amendment adding review for industrial projects failed. Fortune counts over 125 local moratoriums now in place in Ohio.
effects.how: Gives 2027 legislators a clear signal. Many measures are initiative ordinances or advisory, so legal challenges and developer workarounds are the next step.

effects.t: Ohio towns reject rezonings and pass bans, putting projects in doubt
effects.b: At least 14 of 21 Ohio measures passed bans or restrictions, per Fortune. Wilmington voters rejected four rezoning referendums by about 80%. Sunbury passed a charter ban on facilities of 25 MW or more aimed at a possible Amazon project. Trenton's ban likely does not reach the AWS campus already under construction.
effects.how: Rezoning rejections and bans block new projects in these towns. Amazon's Sunbury plan is in doubt.

effects.t: Kansas towns pass three bans, with legal questions ahead
effects.b: Emporia, Ottawa and El Dorado voters approved bans on high-impact data centers. Only El Dorado's is described as a binding mandate. Before the vote, judges in two counties let the questions go forward without ruling on whether voters can set this by petition.
effects.how: Expect court challenges over whether initiative ordinances can ban a land use. No post-election suit has been confirmed.

effects.t: Janesville voters require a public vote on the former GM site
effects.b: The Daily Caller reports more than 60% backed requiring voter approval to redevelop the site, tied to an $8 billion data center proposal. Whether the rule is binding and what it means for the project were not confirmed.
effects.how: If it applies, the developer must win a separate public vote before proceeding.

effects.t: Markets split: hyperscalers up, data center builders down
effects.b: In morning trading Amazon rose about 7%, Microsoft 5.5% and Alphabet 3%, while CoreWeave and Iren fell about 4% each. Analysts called Texas the biggest worry, and one estimated 10 to 15 GW could be affected. Futures dipped on regulation fears, then recovered. Moves are intraday and may reverse.
effects.how: Markets are pricing slower builds for pure-play developers rather than for the large cloud companies, which benefit from scarce capacity.

effects.t: Industry signals conciliation
effects.b: The Data Center Coalition's Texas director said the group wants to work with state leaders, local officials and communities on responsible growth. No hyperscaler or OpenAI statement on the results was found. Musk posted that data centers in space look appealing.
effects.how: Expect industry lobbying to shift toward shaping ratepayer-protection rules rather than fighting them.

effects.t: Exit polling: 56% of voters called AI and data centers a major factor
effects.b: An NBC exit poll cited by Time and CNBC found 56% said the issue was crucial or major in their vote. Early CNN data cited by the Daily Caller showed a wide partisan gap on how crucial it was. Democrats spent over $100 million on broadcast ads tying Republicans to Big Tech.
effects.how: Sets the political baseline for 2027 sessions, though some analysts say the issue mattered less than headlines suggest.

effects.t: Chicago voters back bringing gunshot-detection technology back
effects.b: About 72.5% supported restarting the AI-assisted system the city dropped in 2024, with about 95% of precincts reporting. The question is advisory and leaves the decision to elected officials.
effects.how: Advisory pressure toward AI-based public safety tools; the mayor's administration has already announced a new pilot.
